summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: People in the Interests of M.C.
key_cases.holding: The court reversed an order transferring an Indian child's abuse and neglect proceeding to tribal court, holding that although the tribe's motion was timely, the party opposing transfer was entitled to an evidentiary hearing and that the circuit court had to make specific findings on the good-cause factors.
key_cases.relevance: It is South Dakota's foundational ICWA transfer decision - presumptively tribal jurisdiction under 25 U.S.C. 1911(b), the burden on the party opposing transfer, and a mandatory evidentiary hearing with specific findings on each good-cause factor - and it is the parent authority expressly relied on in People ex rel. T.I. and In re E.T.
key_cases.quote: M.C. was entitled to an evidentiary hearing to establish good cause not to transfer jurisdiction to the Tribe.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a finding of good cause to deny the tribe's ICWA transfer motions, holding that the tribe had actual notice, that the State substantially complied with ICWA's notice requirement, and that the motions filed eleven and seventeen months after notice came at an advanced stage of the proceedings.
key_cases.relevance: It is the South Dakota ICWA transfer decision immediately preceding People ex rel. T.I. and the controlling application of the advanced-stage/untimeliness good-cause factor, while also holding that the State's ICWA notice obligation continues after a tribe intervenes and is not satisfied merely when convenient.
key_cases.quote: The Tribe had actual notice of the pending dispositional hearing, and by faxing notice of the hearing to the Tribe, the State substantially complied with ICWA.

key_cases.holding: The court raised the burden on a party opposing an ICWA transfer to clear and convincing evidence of good cause (prospectively), affirmed the denial of transfer because the moving tribe was not the Indian child's tribe, and affirmed termination on qualified expert testimony and proof beyond a reasonable doubt.
key_cases.relevance: This is South Dakota's governing decision on ICWA transfer: presumptive tribal jurisdiction, the burden on the opponent, and the requirement that a single tribe be designated the Indian child's tribe.
key_cases.quote: the standard most consistent with the Act requires clear and convincing evidence of good cause for a state court to refuse to transfer to tribal court

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the final dispositional order and remanded, holding the circuit court abused its discretion by denying the mother's and the tribe's ICWA transfer motions without an evidentiary hearing and without specific factual findings on good cause.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling South Dakota holding that an ICWA transfer motion cannot be denied on argument alone - a hearing and written findings are required.
key_cases.quote: The circuit court was required to conduct an evidentiary hearing on the question whether good cause existed to deny Mother's and the Tribe's motions to transfer

key_cases.holding: The court held the circuit court abused its discretion by granting a tribe's late oral transfer motion without hearing the available testimony of the child's physician, and reversed for a properly developed record on good cause.
key_cases.relevance: It is the converse of A.O.: a transfer granted on a thin record is as reversible as a transfer denied on one, so the record requirement cuts both ways.
key_cases.quote: circuit courts need the benefit of a sufficiently developed record to assist in the good cause determination

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Dependency and Neglect of A.L.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of a tribe's petition to transfer a dependency and neglect proceeding, holding that the BIA good-cause guidelines are interpretive rather than binding and that the trial court was not clearly erroneous in finding the tribe's transfer request, made a year after notice, untimely.
key_cases.relevance: It is South Dakota's earliest construction of ICWA's undefined 'good cause to the contrary' and the source of the rule, relied on in 2011 S.D. 8 and In the Interest of D.M., that the BIA guidelines inform but do not bind the court and that timeliness is judged case by case.
key_cases.quote: We agree with State that the BIA guidelines are not binding. They are interpretative rather than legislative in nature.
